concern.concern: The framed double-point resolution says: “Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class.” It does not require transport through a small deformation of the original branchwise section, or otherwise specify the relative homotopy class of that extension. Extensions agreeing outside a resolution ball can differ by an arbitrary full normal twist on a branch interval. Twisting only the positive resolution changes its self-linking by one and therefore changes the proposed finite difference. As written, the extension instruction does not uniquely determine the framed derivative; this affects the framed type definition and downstream self-linking witness.

original_concerns.reason: Fixing a section outside a resolution ball does not fix its relative class on the moved interval: in a local trivialized normal2-plane, rotate a nonzero section once through2pi on the interval while fixing endpoint germs. That produces a full relative twist. Permitting it in only one sign resolution changes self-linking by1, so the alternating framed derivative is not determined by the present extension instruction. The fixed round metric already present in the Definition supplies a canonical small transport: short-geodesic parallel transport followed by normal projection. Uniform smallness and nonvanishing near the finitely many double-point preimages keep the section nonzero; a continuous small family keeps the relative homotopy class fixed. This completes the intended framed interface without deleting framed singularities, zero resolutions, type statements or any resolved proof.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: Resolve each double point by a sufficiently $C^1$-small separation of its two parameter branches, fixed outside the chosen ball. Use the fixed round metric to represent the original normal section orthogonally to the original tangent. Parallel-transport that vector along the unique short round-metric geodesic from the original branch point to its resolved point, and then project orthogonally to the normal plane of the resolved tangent. The section is nonzero near the double-point preimages, so for sufficiently small separations these projections remain nonzero and agree with the old section outside the ball. This prescribes the relative homotopy class of the transported section: no independent full normal twist may be inserted in a resolution ball. A homotopy through such small separations gives a homotopy through nonzero projected sections. Once the framing zeroes are also resolved as below, the resulting nonzero section determines a framing homotopy class.
